476.t: After Desdunes: Buddy Bo, and Harry's own band
476.s: Back home Harry played with Buddy Bo, then led his own band with Eddie Palud, Eddie Thomas and Harold, playing weekends while holding a day job.
476.q: Yeah. And it looked like, sometime he looked like he was sucking in on that trumpet and blowing. Really? That's the truth. I never saw that. Yeah, you had a pair of chops out of this world. Well didn't we forget somebody? Didn't we forget somebody? David Jones? David Jones? No, David Jones didn't…

510.t: Forming Stone Alliance with Gene Perla
510.s: Stone Alliance began among close friends at his mother's house; Perla did business, Alias was musical director, playing rock-jazz with Steve Grossman and later Kenny Kirkland.
510.ch: Own bands and the England tour
510.q: Well I remember Tony Williams, I can always — I had such great teachers, and they would say like a couple of sentences and they would show you the road you know. Tony had this group called Ego that was out. And he was really like depressed and everything. And he just said “when you get your own…

898.t: First Vanguard week as a leader with Carter, Barron and Nash
898.s: He assembled Ron Carter, Kenny Barron and Lewis Nash to win a Village Vanguard week and called Elvin for his first record.
898.q: I’ve never had a club owner tell me a musical prowess such as that, but I’ve had club owners asking is there a way that we could beef up the lineup. Now, the first gig I ever had in my life, in New York as a leader was at the Village Vanguard. I went up to the owner, Lorraine Gordon, and said, “I’d…

159.t: Becoming a leader and recording 'Just Plain Junior' for Verve
159.s: He considered leading around 1961; Norman Granz offered him an album while with Dizzy, with Ray Brown on bass.
159.ch: Going solo and the Dizzy Gillespie years
159.q: Yeah. That was years later though after Gene Ammons. I think it was about 1961 that I gave serious thought to becoming a leader. Because I made my first record as a leader in ’58 or ’59, it was a Verve record called “Just Plain Junior.” I was playing with Dizzy at the time. And Norman Granz, who…

396.t: Finding her own gigs as a leader before being called as a sideperson
396.s: She led her own quartet and big band for many years before being hired as a sideperson.
396.q: I would say yes. Yes. Finding them myself and what you’re saying is exactly right. I mean I don’t think, as I remember it, I didn’t get called as a sideperson for many years following forming my own groups and being leader and playing as leader of a quartet or big band or whatever. Then, after many…

225.t: Preparing his first date as a leader and choosing players
225.s: After a break he discusses the responsibility of leading and choosing Max Roach, Bud Powell and others by word of mouth.
225.q: As I recall it, Lida, my first exposure as a leader was – it was a small combo. But even that early on, I became aware of the responsibility that that role carries with it. At first it didn’t seem such a heavyweight issue, but the more I began to prepare for the realization of this recording, I…

377.t: Why he started a band of his own
377.s: Basie says he just wanted to try leading, having had a band in Little Rock.
377.ch: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
377.q: Because -- I don't know. I just wanted to do something on my own, because I had had a band before. I had a band (inaudible) had a band at Little Rock. (Inaudible).

758.s: Roy had a big band in 1943 and no longer booked with Glaser.
758.q: : Let me see, did I start my own band again? I had a band in '43, didn't I. So it must have been there. That's when I started that band, yeah. The (?)Fish Market(?)

385.t: Leading his own group on 52nd Street; the Blue Note recordings
385.s: After Tatum he led a quartet then a sextet with Trummy Young and John Hardee, and recorded Flying Home for Blue Note.
385.ch: Chords, recordings and his own groups
385.q: -- Well I had this little trio, can't even count that, that's not even counted as far as jazz, that little Wynken Blynken and Nod thing. That was a step in the right direction I guess you'd say. But my first little group of my own was right on 52nd St. Right after the Tatum thing broke up. And I…

235.t: Leaving Dizzy to lead his own band
235.s: Soon after returning he formed his own group, taking small jobs and learning to get work and be a business man before the Paradise.
235.ch: Back in New York: Heard and Dizzy
235.q: : Yeah, not much longer after that. And what I decided then that I should get my own band, you know what I mean. I got my own band and started workin' little jobs and I began to learn about how to get a job and things was a new experience and bein' a leader, you know what I mean.

124.t: Whether McRae led bands of his own
124.s: He says the McRae Brothers was his only early band and that he led big bands in 1945-47.
124.ch: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
124.q: After I had left -- I think it was Cab, or somebody like that. '45 or '47, I had a couple of bands, big bands that I had put together.
